analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of docs/threat-model.yaml, the complete changed-range map, bounded patch, canonical definition index and supplied T-041 detail. No concrete regression is established by these BASE-only units. Most visible text is unchanged: cache confidentiality/scoping and purge constraints (1396–1466), legacy attestation/replay protections (1468–1760), update recovery (1762–1830), privileged fan authority (1832–1977), memory-only media ingestion (1979–2041), and App Attest authorization, billing, qualification and diagnostic boundaries (2043–2304). Their documented residual risks are not new findings.
The relevant changed BASE mitigation is T-059 at 2323–2327: signed audit-token peers, bounded socket admission, leases/machine-lock fallback, persisted holds, and drain ownership across updates/reconnects protect A-018 at TB-012. The partial patch expands TB-012 to an operator mailbox and announces accept-time checks, socket overrides, fail-open records, a model-load fence and new T-060 availability coverage; announcements alone do not establish implemented controls or vulnerabilities.
Integration must compare HEAD TB-012 (820–862), T-059 (2349–2365) and T-060 (2366–2398) with the changed add-on IPC, lifecycle mailbox, control-file readers and model-loading paths. Verify unauthorized clients cannot consume admission capacity before peer validation, control-file reads cannot stall serving/control dispatch, and hold failure/release cannot reopen model loading during VM use. Coordinator busy-field enforcement remains an external contract, not an observed missing control. HEAD definitions and executable changes are absent from this batch, leaving these PR-specific security conclusions unresolved.
